107: \(\lambda!\), \(j!\), \((\lambda-j)!\) is divisible by \(p\), so
108: \(\binom\lambda j\) is a unit in \(R\). Consequently
109: 
110: \[
111: E_{ij}=\left(\binom\lambda j\right)^{-1}
112:        X_{\lambda-i}P Y_{\lambda-j}.                 \tag{2}
113: \]
114: 
115: Every matrix unit preserves \(M_R\). No assertion about distinct
116: weights modulo \(p\) has been used.
117: 
118: ### 3. Recover a standard basis for the arbitrary lattice
119: 
120: Define \(J_i=\{c\in\mathbb C:c e_i\in M_R\}\).
121: The coordinate projection \(E_{ii}\) maps \(M_R\) onto \(J_i e_i\).
122: Applying \(E_{ij}\) to \(c e_j\) shows \(J_j\subseteq J_i\);
123: reversing the indices gives equality. Let \(J\) be their common module.
124: It is finitely generated, being a projection of a finite free module,
125: and nonzero because \(M_R\) spans \(V(\lambda)\) over \(\mathbb C\).
126: The coordinate projections and independence of the \(e_i\) give
127: 
128: \[
129: M_R=\bigoplus_{i=0}^{\lambda}J e_i.                  \tag{3}
130: \]
131: 
132: One must still prove that \(J\) has rank one; containment in
133: \(\mathbb C\) alone does not imply that. Let
134: \(r=\dim_{\mathbb Q}(\mathbb Q\otimes_R J)\), which is finite.
135: Tensoring (3) with the fraction field \(\mathbb Q\) and using the
136: rank \(n\) of \(M_R\) gives \(n=nr\), so \(r=1\), since \(n>0\).
137: The multiplication map \(\mathbb Q\otimes_R J\to\mathbb C\) is
138: injective: this tensor product is the localization of the torsion-free
139: module \(J\subset\mathbb C\), and a fraction mapping to zero has
140: zero numerator. Thus \(J\) spans a one-dimensional rational line.
141: 
142: Choose \(0\ne a\in J\) and write a finite set of nonzero generators
143: as \(q_1a,\ldots,q_ka\) with \(q_j\in\mathbb Q^\times\).
144: Each \(q_j=p^{\nu_j}u_j\) for \(\nu_j\in\mathbb Z\) and a unit
145: \(u_j\) of \(R\). Let \(\nu=\min_j\nu_j\). All generators belong
146: to \(p^\nu R a\), and a generator with minimal exponent generates
147: that whole module. Therefore \(J=Rb\) for a nonzero \(b\in J\).
148: By (3), \(b e_0,\ldots,b e_\lambda\) is an \(R\)-basis of \(M_R\).
149: 
150: ### 4. Reduce and extend scalars
151: 
152: All denominators in \(R\) are invertible in \(K\), so the integer map
153: extends to \(R\to K\). The natural tensor maps give
154: 
155: \[
156: M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\cong M_R\otimes_R K
157: \cong(M_R/pM_R)\otimes_{\mathbb F_p}K.
158: \]
159: 
160: For example the first map sends \(m\otimes c\) to
161: \((1\otimes m)\otimes c\); its inverse sends
162: \((r\otimes m)\otimes c\) to \(m\otimes\bar r c\).
163: The reduced images \(b_0,\ldots,b_\lambda\) of \(b e_i\) form a
164: \(K\)-basis, with exactly the matrices of step 1 reduced into \(K\).
165: The matrix-unit identities (2) persist on this basis.
166: 
167: For \(0\leq r\leq\lambda<p\), \(r!\ne0\) in \(K\), and the induced
168: \(X_r,Y_r\) equal \((r!)^{-1}x^r,(r!)^{-1}y^r\). Hence any
169: \(K\)-subspace invariant under \(x,y\) is invariant under every matrix
170: unit in (2).
171: 
172: ### 5. Conclude irreducibility
173: 
174: Let \(W\) be invariant. If it is nonzero, choose
175: \(0\ne w=\sum_i c_i b_i\in W\), and an index \(j\) with \(c_j\ne0\).
176: For every \(i\), \(E_{ij}w=c_jb_i\in W\). Division by \(c_j\)
177: gives \(b_i\in W\), so all basis vectors lie in \(W\) and
178: \(W=V(K)\). Since \(\dim_K V(K)=\lambda+1>0\), it is nonzero and
179: irreducible. If \(\lambda=0\), all relevant factorials and binomial
180: coefficients are one and the argument applies unchanged. For \(p=2\),
181: the allowed \(\lambda\) are zero and one; the proof still works
182: without requiring distinct reduced \(h\)-eigenvalues.

102: 
103: For the last identity, an input index below \(j\) is sent below
104: \(e_\lambda\) and killed by \(P\); an index above \(j\) is sent past
105: the end of the lowering string. On \(e_j\) the coefficient is precisely
106: \(\binom\lambda j\). Since \(\lambda<p\), none of
107: \(\lambda!\), \(j!\), \((\lambda-j)!\) is divisible by \(p\), so
108: \(\binom\lambda j\) is a unit in \(R\). Consequently
109: 
110: \[
111: E_{ij}=\left(\binom\lambda j\right)^{-1}
112:        X_{\lambda-i}P Y_{\lambda-j}.                 \tag{2}
113: \]
114: 
115: Every matrix unit preserves \(M_R\). No assertion about distinct
116: weights modulo \(p\) has been used.
117: 
118: ### 3. Recover a standard basis for the arbitrary lattice
119: 
120: Define \(J_i=\{c\in\mathbb C:c e_i\in M_R\}\).
121: The coordinate projection \(E_{ii}\) maps \(M_R\) onto \(J_i e_i\).
122: Applying \(E_{ij}\) to \(c e_j\) shows \(J_j\subseteq J_i\);
123: reversing the indices gives equality. Let \(J\) be their common module.
124: It is finitely generated, being a projection of a finite free module,
125: and nonzero because \(M_R\) spans \(V(\lambda)\) over \(\mathbb C\).
126: The coordinate projections and independence of the \(e_i\) give
127: 
128: \[
129: M_R=\bigoplus_{i=0}^{\lambda}J e_i.                  \tag{3}
130: \]
131: 
132: One must still prove that \(J\) has rank one; containment in
133: \(\mathbb C\) alone does not imply that. Let
134: \(r=\dim_{\mathbb Q}(\mathbb Q\otimes_R J)\), which is finite.
135: Tensoring (3) with the fraction field \(\mathbb Q\) and using the
136: rank \(n\) of \(M_R\) gives \(n=nr\), so \(r=1\), since \(n>0\).
137: The multiplication map \(\mathbb Q\otimes_R J\to\mathbb C\) is
138: injective: this tensor product is the localization of the torsion-free
139: module \(J\subset\mathbb C\), and a fraction mapping to zero has
140: zero numerator. Thus \(J\) spans a one-dimensional rational line.
141: 
142: Choose \(0\ne a\in J\) and write a finite set of nonzero generators
143: as \(q_1a,\ldots,q_ka\) with \(q_j\in\mathbb Q^\times\).
144: Each \(q_j=p^{\nu_j}u_j\) for \(\nu_j\in\mathbb Z\) and a unit
145: \(u_j\) of \(R\). Let \(\nu=\min_j\nu_j\). All generators belong
146: to \(p^\nu R a\), and a generator with minimal exponent generates
147: that whole module. Therefore \(J=Rb\) for a nonzero \(b\in J\).
148: By (3), \(b e_0,\ldots,b e_\lambda\) is an \(R\)-basis of \(M_R\).
149: 
150: ### 4. Reduce and extend scalars
151: 
152: All denominators in \(R\) are invertible in \(K\), so the integer map
153: extends to \(R\to K\). The natural tensor maps give
154: 
155: \[
156: M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\cong M_R\otimes_R K
157: \cong(M_R/pM_R)\otimes_{\mathbb F_p}K.
158: \]
159: 
160: For example the first map sends \(m\otimes c\) to
161: \((1\otimes m)\otimes c\); its inverse sends
162: \((r\otimes m)\otimes c\) to \(m\otimes\bar r c\).
163: The reduced images \(b_0,\ldots,b_\lambda\) of \(b e_i\) form a
164: \(K\)-basis, with exactly the matrices of step 1 reduced into \(K\).
165: The matrix-unit identities (2) persist on this basis.
166: 
167: For \(0\leq r\leq\lambda<p\), \(r!\ne0\) in \(K\), and the induced
168: \(X_r,Y_r\) equal \((r!)^{-1}x^r,(r!)^{-1}y^r\). Hence any
169: \(K\)-subspace invariant under \(x,y\) is invariant under every matrix
170: unit in (2).
171: 
172: ### 5. Conclude irreducibility
173: 
174: Let \(W\) be invariant. If it is nonzero, choose
175: \(0\ne w=\sum_i c_i b_i\in W\), and an index \(j\) with \(c_j\ne0\).
176: For every \(i\), \(E_{ij}w=c_jb_i\in W\). Division by \(c_j\)
177: gives \(b_i\in W\), so all basis vectors lie in \(W\) and
178: \(W=V(K)\). Since \(\dim_K V(K)=\lambda+1>0\), it is nonzero and
179: irreducible. If \(\lambda=0\), all relevant factorials and binomial
180: coefficients are one and the argument applies unchanged. For \(p=2\),
181: the allowed \(\lambda\) are zero and one; the proof still works
182: without requiring distinct reduced \(h\)-eigenvalues.

3: namespace YuiObjects

5: noncomputable def dividedPower {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
6:     (a : Module.End ℂ V) (r : ℕ) : Module.End ℂ V :=
7:   ((Nat.factorial r : ℂ)⁻¹) • (a ^ r)
8: 
9: def stable {F V : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup V] [Module F V]
10:     (a : Module.End F V) (W : Submodule F V) : Prop :=
11:   ∀ w ∈ W, a w ∈ W
12: 
13: def highestWeightData {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
14:     (lam : ℕ) (h x y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
15:   v ≠ 0 ∧ x v = 0 ∧ h v = (lam : ℂ) • v ∧
16:   h * x - x * h = (2 : ℂ) • x ∧
17:   h * y - y * h = (-2 : ℂ) • y ∧
18:   x * y - y * x = h ∧ Module.finrank ℂ V = lam + 1
19: 
20: def admissibleLattice {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
21:     (lam : ℕ) (x y : Module.End ℂ V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
22:   (∃ (b : Module.Basis (Fin (lam + 1)) ℤ M)
23:       (e : Module.Basis (Fin (lam + 1)) ℂ V), ∀ i, (b i : V) = e i) ∧
24:   (∀ (r : ℕ) (m : M), dividedPower x r (m : V) ∈ M) ∧
25:   (∀ (r : ℕ) (m : M), dividedPower y r (m : V) ∈ M)
26: 
27: def matrixUnits {F V I : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup V] [Module F V]
28:     [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] (f : I → I → Module.End F V) : Prop :=
29:   (∀ i j k l, f i j * f k l = if j = k then f i l else 0) ∧
30:   (∑ i, f i i) = 1
31: 
32: end YuiObjects
33: 
34: namespace YuiObjects
35: noncomputable def latticeEnd {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
36:     (M : Submodule ℤ V) (f : Module.End ℂ V) : Module.End ℤ M :=
37:   @dite (Module.End ℤ M) (∀ z ∈ M, f z ∈ M)
38:     (Classical.propDecidable _) (fun hs => (f.restrictScalars ℤ).restrict hs) (fun _ => 0)
39: end YuiObjects
40: 
41: universe uK uV
42: namespace YuiObjects
43: abbrev ell (lam : ℤ) : ℕ := lam.toNat
44: abbrev Idx (lam : ℤ) := Fin (ell lam + 1)
45: noncomputable def ev {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
46:     (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : V := dividedPower y i v
47: def coeff (lam : ℤ) (j : Idx lam) : ℕ := Nat.choose (ell lam) j.val
48: def coeffProd (lam : ℤ) : ℕ := ∏ j : Idx lam, coeff lam j
49: def coeffOmit (lam : ℤ) (i : Idx lam) : ℕ :=
50:   ∏ j ∈ (Finset.univ.erase i), coeff lam j
51: noncomputable def projector {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
52:     (lam : ℤ) (x y : Module.End ℂ V) : Module.End ℂ V :=
53:   dividedPower y (ell lam) * dividedPower x (ell lam)
54: noncomputable def integralMatrix {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
55:     (lam : ℤ) (x y : Module.End ℂ V) (i j : Idx lam) : Module.End ℂ V :=

3: Apply these requirements within the accepted NL0 and the fixed Lean interface.

6: model, new premise or mandatory lookup of every familiar declaration is needed.
7: 
8: 1. **Check critical library signatures.** Before relying on a critical or
9:    unfamiliar library application, establish its complete type in the pinned
10:    environment, including explicit, implicit and instance binders and all
11:    side conditions. Read the declaration or check a small typed application
12:    when its signature is uncertain. Do not infer the calling convention from
13:    its name or pass an implicit argument as though it were an explicit one.
14:    A previously checked signature in this context need not be looked up again.
15: 2. **Constrain difficult inference.** When coercions or implicit inference
16:    obscure the intended application, give the intermediate fact an explicit
17:    type and supply the relevant named parameters, such as the set, exponent
18:    or ambient space. Prefer this to leaving Lean to discover those choices by
19:    unfolding large definitions. Routine unambiguous arguments can stay
20:    implicit; explicit parameters must preserve the existing target and inputs.
21: 3. **Check conversions before combining them.** When an argument crosses Lean
22:    representations, first establish a small typed conversion fact, then use
23:    it in the main proof. In particular, distinguish `ℝ`, `ℝ≥0` and `ℝ≥0∞`;
24:    check the conversion direction, nonnegativity and any finiteness conditions.
25:    A conversion is not automatically invertible, and matching notation does
26:    not establish equality of differently typed expressions. Reuse a checked
27:    fact when available. Do not invent another representation, a global helper
28:    requirement or an extra hypothesis just to satisfy this instruction.
29: 4. **Isolate an inference failure.** If compiler feedback identifies a library
30:    application, coercion or expensive inference problem, reduce the next check
31:    to that application or conversion with explicit local types before adding
32:    more proof code. Use `check_auxiliary` in a proof worker, or
33:    `check_lean_types` during preparation when that tool is supplied. Helpers
34:    use only the current allowed inputs and never become new premises. Once
35:    the small check succeeds, integrate the result and recheck the complete
36:    obligation; success of a helper alone does not accept the target.
37: 
38: 5. **Repair after a bounded check.** Native checks have a separate per-call wall
39:    limit, normally 180 seconds, and use the controller-owned 20,000,000 heartbeat budget.
40:    A timeout or heartbeat diagnostic leaves the goal unaccepted and returns
41:    control to the same worker. Inspect the retained candidate and diagnostic,

2: 
3: Apply these requirements within the accepted NL0 and the fixed Lean interface.
4: They govern implementation, not additional NL0 detail or a weaker Audit B.
5: Use existing library readers and local checking tools; no separate review
6: model, new premise or mandatory lookup of every familiar declaration is needed.
7: 
8: 1. **Check critical library signatures.** Before relying on a critical or
9:    unfamiliar library application, establish its complete type in the pinned
10:    environment, including explicit, implicit and instance binders and all
11:    side conditions. Read the declaration or check a small typed application
12:    when its signature is uncertain. Do not infer the calling convention from
13:    its name or pass an implicit argument as though it were an explicit one.
14:    A previously checked signature in this context need not be looked up again.
15: 2. **Constrain difficult inference.** When coercions or implicit inference
16:    obscure the intended application, give the intermediate fact an explicit
17:    type and supply the relevant named parameters, such as the set, exponent
18:    or ambient space. Prefer this to leaving Lean to discover those choices by
19:    unfolding large definitions. Routine unambiguous arguments can stay
20:    implicit; explicit parameters must preserve the existing target and inputs.
21: 3. **Check conversions before combining them.** When an argument crosses Lean
22:    representations, first establish a small typed conversion fact, then use
23:    it in the main proof. In particular, distinguish `ℝ`, `ℝ≥0` and `ℝ≥0∞`;
24:    check the conversion direction, nonnegativity and any finiteness conditions.
25:    A conversion is not automatically invertible, and matching notation does
26:    not establish equality of differently typed expressions. Reuse a checked
27:    fact when available. Do not invent another representation, a global helper
28:    requirement or an extra hypothesis just to satisfy this instruction.
29: 4. **Isolate an inference failure.** If compiler feedback identifies a library
30:    application, coercion or expensive inference problem, reduce the next check
31:    to that application or conversion with explicit local types before adding
32:    more proof code. Use `check_auxiliary` in a proof worker, or
33:    `check_lean_types` during preparation when that tool is supplied. Helpers
34:    use only the current allowed inputs and never become new premises. Once
35:    the small check succeeds, integrate the result and recheck the complete
36:    obligation; success of a helper alone does not accept the target.
37: 
38: 5. **Repair after a bounded check.** Native checks have a separate per-call wall
39:    limit, normally 180 seconds, and use the controller-owned 20,000,000 heartbeat budget.
40:    A timeout or heartbeat diagnostic leaves the goal unaccepted and returns
41:    control to the same worker. Inspect the retained candidate and diagnostic,
42:    then check a smaller typed application, conversion or proof fragment before
43:    integrating it. Do not repeat the unchanged expensive candidate or disable
44:    limits to avoid diagnosis. Preserve the target, allowed inputs and proof
45:    requirements; a timeout alone establishes no mathematical gap.

47: The runtime enforces the per-call wall limit independently of these writing
48: rules. Whole-case and model-stage execution remain unlimited by default.
49: Retain failed attempts and actual diagnostics. Standalone assembly, native
50: trust/signature checks and final machine Audit B remain required.
51: 
52: Before freeze, every complete T declaration must elaborate with exactly its

54: that their argument types cannot determine; a same-named context variable is

61: application with the existing local parameters/inputs. Reuse these theorems in
62: later auxiliary checks and the final body. The controller retains their actual

65: context reset; never rebuild a checked helper merely because a turn ended.
66:

Scope and representations.
Keep all original hypotheses: p is any prime; K is any field of characteristic p; λ is an integer with 0≤λ<p; V=V(λ) is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂-module of dimension λ+1; the generators obey [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=−2y, [x,y]=h; 0≠v has xv=0 and hv=λv; and M is ANY admissible lattice stable under the integer algebra generated by every X_r=x^r/r!, Y_r=y^r/r!, r≥0. There is no extra assumption on K. There is no algorithm or constant-dependence specification to alter.

Use λ also for its natural-number representative (since it is nonnegative), with the same integer value in scalar coefficients, and set n=λ+1>0 and I={0,...,λ}, formally Fin(n). Returning to the original integer parameter is the identity λ=(Int.toNat λ:ℤ). All occurrences of factorials, binomial coefficients and index subtraction below have natural arguments; λ−2i in a scalar weight denotes integer subtraction, not truncated natural subtraction.

View the original free abelian subgroup M as its ℤ-submodule in V. Its inclusion ι:M→V is injective. An integer basis that is also a complex basis has exactly n elements: the latter basis has cardinal n by the given complex dimension. Reindex it by I. Thus the header predicate admissibleLattice is exactly an encoding of the original lattice condition: it asserts such paired bases and stability under all divided powers. Stability under their generated ℤ-algebra follows by sums, integer multiples and compositions, so is equivalent to the stated U_ℤ-stability. B002 says a linearly independent family of the same finite cardinality as the dimension spans.

B101. Derive the characteristic-zero strings and all required coordinates.

Indeed the h induction subtracts 2 from the weight each time. If x t_r=r(λ−r+1)t_{r−1}, then

The same computation starts at r=0 using xv=0, hv=λv. Scalar coefficients here are in ℂ, with integer arithmetic.

For 0≤i≤λ, iteration of this formula gives
  x^i t_i = [∏_{s=1}^i s(λ−s+1)]v

Each factor is a positive integer, hence a nonzero complex number, and v≠0. For i=0 the product is 1. Thus t_i≠0. Put e_i=t_i/i!; these are nonzero eigenvectors of h with weights λ−2i. These weights are injectively indexed over ℂ, since equality gives 2(i−j)=0 and characteristic zero gives i=j. B001 proves their linear independence; B002 and dim V=n show they span. It remains to justify termination rather than assume it. The vector t_{λ+1} has weight −λ−2 by the same h induction. Write it uniquely in the spanning independent family e_i. Its eigenvector equation gives that its i-th coefficient times
  (λ−2i)−(−λ−2)=2(λ+1−i)
is zero. This factor is a nonzero complex number for every i≤λ. Every coefficient is zero, so t_{λ+1}=0. All further t_r vanish by another application of y.

  y e_i=(i+1)e_{i+1} (i<λ); y e_λ=0;
  h e_i=(λ−2i)e_i.
Iteration gives, for all natural r,
  X_r e_i=binom(λ−i+r,r)e_{i−r} if r≤i, and 0 if r>i;
  Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_{i+r} if i+r≤λ, and 0 otherwise.
For the first nonzero case the numerator accumulated by x^r is

def stable {F V : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup V] [Module F V]
    (a : Module.End F V) (W : Submodule F V) : Prop :=

def highestWeightData {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (lam : ℕ) (h x y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  v ≠ 0 ∧ x v = 0 ∧ h v = (lam : ℂ) • v ∧
  h * x - x * h = (2 : ℂ) • x ∧
  h * y - y * h = (-2 : ℂ) • y ∧
  x * y - y * x = h ∧ Module.finrank ℂ V = lam + 1

    (lam : ℕ) (x y : Module.End ℂ V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=

    [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] (f : I → I → Module.End F V) : Prop :=

end YuiObjects

2: 
3: ## Original exercise
4: 
5: James E. Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*,
6: Graduate Texts in Mathematics 9, Springer, section 27, exercise 7,
7: printed page 164. The exercise-list convention on page 163 sets
8: \(L=\mathfrak{sl}_2\) and identifies weights with integers.
9: Book DOI: [10.1007/978-1-4612-6398-2](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4612-6398-2).
10: 
11: > 7. If \(0\leq\lambda<\operatorname{char}K\), \(V=V(\lambda)\),
12: > prove that \(V(K)\) is irreducible as \(L(K)\)-module.
13: 
14: ## Definitions and complete target
15: 
16: Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
17: \(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
18: Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
19: \(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
20: of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy
21: 
22: \[
23: [h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
24: \]
25: 
26: Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
27: \(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
28: the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
29: \(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
30: An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
31: subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
32: \(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.
33: 
34: Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
35: \(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
36: acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
37: \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
38: Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
39: invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
40: Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
41: algebraically closed.
42: 
43: ## Fixed natural-language proof
44: 
45: ### 1. Divided-power coordinates in characteristic zero
46: 
47: Put \(n=\lambda+1\) and \(e_i=y^iv/i!\) for \(0\leq i\leq\lambda\).
48: The commutator identities give, by induction,
49: 
50: \[
51: hy^iv=(\lambda-2i)y^iv,\qquad
52: xy^iv=i(\lambda-i+1)y^{i-1}v\quad(i\geq1).
53: \]
54: 
55: For \(i\leq\lambda\), applying \(x^i\) to \(y^iv\) gives
56: \(i!\lambda(\lambda-1)\cdots(\lambda-i+1)v\ne0\) over \(\mathbb C\).
57: At \(i=0\) the empty product is one. Thus every \(e_i\ne0\).
58: Their \(h\)-eigenvalues \(\lambda-2i\) are distinct over \(\mathbb C\),
59: so they are linearly independent: applying
60: \(\prod_{k\ne j}(h-(\lambda-2k)\mathrm{Id})\) to a relation isolates
61: its \(j\)-th coefficient with a nonzero multiplier.

66: inductive Eqv : FreeAddMonoid (M × N) → FreeAddMonoid (M × N) → Prop
67:   | of_zero_left : ∀ n : N, Eqv (.of (0, n)) 0
68:   | of_zero_right : ∀ m : M, Eqv (.of (m, 0)) 0
69:   | of_add_left : ∀ (m₁ m₂ : M) (n : N), Eqv (.of (m₁, n) + .of (m₂, n)) (.of (m₁ + m₂, n))
70:   | of_add_right : ∀ (m : M) (n₁ n₂ : N), Eqv (.of (m, n₁) + .of (m, n₂)) (.of (m, n₁ + n₂))
71:   | of_smul : ∀ (r : R) (m : M) (n : N), Eqv (.of (r • m, n)) (.of (m, r • n))
72:   | add_comm : ∀ x y, Eqv (x + y) (y + x)
73: 
74: end

76: end TensorProduct

79: /-- The tensor product of two modules `M` and `N` over the same commutative semiring `R`.

47: section Semiring
48: 
49: /-- The rank of a module as a natural number.
50: 
51: For a finite-dimensional vector space `V` over a field `k`, `Module.finrank k V` is equal to
52: the dimension of `V` over `k`.
53: 
54: For a general module `M` over a ring `R`, `Module.finrank R M` is defined to be the supremum of the
55: cardinalities of the `R`-linearly independent subsets of `M`, if this supremum is finite. It is
56: defined by convention to be `0` if this supremum is infinite. See `Module.rank` for a
57: cardinal-valued version where infinite rank modules have rank an infinite cardinal.
58: 
59: Note that if `R` is not a field then there can exist modules `M` with `¬(Module.Finite R M)` but
60: `finrank R M ≠ 0`. For example `ℚ` has `finrank` equal to `1` over `ℤ`, because the nonempty
61: `ℤ`-linearly independent subsets of `ℚ` are precisely the nonzero singletons. -/
62: noncomputable def finrank (R M : Type*) [Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] : ℕ :=
63:   Cardinal.toNat (Module.rank R M)
64: 
65: @[simp] theorem finrank_subsingleton [Subsingleton R] : finrank R M = 1 := by
66:   rw [finrank, rank_subsingleton, map_one]

{"id": "spec.json", "pointer": "/full_target", "view": "string", "offset": 0, "end_offset": 1263, "total_chars": 1263, "has_more": false, "next_offset": null, "value": "Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed."}

{"id": "contract.json", "pointer": "/header", "view": "string", "offset": 0, "end_offset": 3578, "total_chars": 3578, "has_more": false, "next_offset": null, "value": "import Mathlib

namespace YuiObjects

noncomputable def dividedPower {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (a : Module.End ℂ V) (r : ℕ) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  ((Nat.factorial r : ℂ)⁻¹) • (a ^ r)

def stable {F V : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup V] [Module F V]
    (a : Module.End F V) (W : Submodule F V) : Prop :=
  ∀ w ∈ W, a w ∈ W

def highestWeightData {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (lam : ℕ) (h x y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  v ≠ 0 ∧ x v = 0 ∧ h v = (lam : ℂ) • v ∧
  h * x - x * h = (2 : ℂ) • x ∧
  h * y - y * h = (-2 : ℂ) • y ∧
  x * y - y * x = h ∧ Module.finrank ℂ V = lam + 1

def admissibleLattice {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (lam : ℕ) (x y : Module.End ℂ V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  (∃ (b : Module.Basis (Fin (lam + 1)) ℤ M)
      (e : Module.Basis (Fin (lam + 1)) ℂ V), ∀ i, (b i : V) = e i) ∧
  (∀ (r : ℕ) (m : M), dividedPower x r (m : V) ∈ M) ∧
  (∀ (r : ℕ) (m : M), dividedPower y r (m : V) ∈ M)

def matrixUnits {F V I : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup V] [Module F V]
    [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] (f : I → I → Module.End F V) : Prop :=
  (∀ i j k l, f i j * f k l = if j = k then f i l else 0) ∧
  (∑ i, f i i) = 1

end YuiObjects

namespace YuiObjects
noncomputable def latticeEnd {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (M : Submodule ℤ V) (f : Module.End ℂ V) : Module.End ℤ M :=
  @dite (Module.End ℤ M) (∀ z ∈ M, f z ∈ M)
    (Classical.propDecidable _) (fun hs => (f.restrictScalars ℤ).restrict hs) (fun _ => 0)
end YuiObjects

universe uK uV
namespace YuiObjects
abbrev ell (lam : ℤ) : ℕ := lam.toNat
abbrev Idx (lam : ℤ) := Fin (ell lam + 1)
noncomputable def ev {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : V := dividedPower y i v
def coeff (lam : ℤ) (j : Idx lam) : ℕ := Nat.choose (ell lam) j.val
def coeffProd (lam : ℤ) : ℕ := ∏ j : Idx lam, coeff lam j
def coeffOmit (lam : ℤ) (i : Idx lam) : ℕ :=
  ∏ j ∈ (Finset.univ.erase i), coeff lam j
noncomputable def projector {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (lam : ℤ) (x y : Module.End ℂ V) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  dividedPower y (ell lam) * dividedPower x (ell lam)
noncomputable def integralMatrix {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (lam : ℤ) (x y : Module.End ℂ V) (i j : Idx lam) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  dividedPower x (ell lam - i.val) * projector lam x y *
    dividedPower y (ell lam - j.val)
abbrev TensorLeft (K M : Type*) [Field K] [AddCommGroup M] := TensorProduct ℤ K M
abbrev TensorRight (K M : Type*) [Field K] [AddCommGroup M] := TensorProduct ℤ M K
noncomputable instance rightTensorModule (K M : Type*) [Field K] [AddCommGroup M] :
    Module K (TensorRight K M) :=
  (TensorProduct.comm ℤ M K).toAddEquiv.module K
noncomputable def tensorSwap (K M : Type*) [Field K] [AddCommGroup M] :
    TensorRight K M ≃ₗ[K] TensorLeft K M :=
  (TensorProduct.comm ℤ M K).toAddEquiv.linearEquiv K
noncomputable def hat {K M : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup M]
    (f : Module.End ℤ M) : Module.End K (TensorLeft K M) := f.baseChange K
noncomputable def induced {K M : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup M]
    (f : Module.End ℤ M) : Module.End K (TensorRight K M) :=
  (tensorSwap K M).symm.toLinearMap.comp ((hat (K := K) f).comp (tensorSwap K M).toLinearMap)
noncomputable def scaledMatrix {K V : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (lam : ℤ) (x y : Module.End ℂ V) (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (i j : Idx lam) : Module.End K (TensorLeft K M) :=
  ((coeff lam j : K)⁻¹) • hat (K := K) (latticeEnd M (integralMatrix lam x y i j))
end YuiObjects
open YuiObjects
"}

parameters_and_allowed_inputs.notes: The actual __signature_P quantifies p:ℕ, K:Type uK with Field K, lam:ℤ, V:Type uV with AddCommGroup V and Module ℂ V, three complex-linear endomorphisms, v:V and M:Submodule ℤ V, followed by exactly H001–H006. Nat.Prime p and CharP K p retain primality and characteristic; 0≤lam∧lam<(p:ℤ) retains the complete integer interval. H004 includes explicit FiniteDimensional ℂ V, the integer-valued dimension equation, and complex generator-invariant-subspace irreducibility. Jointly with H005's nonzero highest-weight vector and all three Chevalley commutators, these encode the original highest-weight sl₂ representation in both directions: the generators determine its action and their linear span determines invariant subspaces. No irreducibility hypothesis was transferred from ℂ to K. H006's paired ℤ/ℂ bases are arbitrary, not the divided-power string basis. Its Fin(ell+1) indexing follows from H003/H004 by reindexing any original paired basis; conversely such a finite paired basis is an original admissible lattice basis. Stability under every divided power is equivalent to stability under the generated integer algebra. No rationality of v, minimality, algebraic closure, nonzero h, p>2 or lam>0 is imposed. The domain is not vacuous, including lam=0. Characteristic and prime instances needed by library applications are explicitly planned to be installed from H001/H002. Private preflight False binders occur only in diagnostic declarations, not in __signature_P or the proposed worker inputs.

representations_and_conversion_obligatio.notes: Unfolded all endpoint-relevant header definitions and verified the correspondence claims. ell=lam.toNat is identified with lam only under nonnegativity; Idx=Fin(ell+1) includes both endpoints and is nonempty. Scalar weights subtract in ℂ after casting, agreeing with the specified integer subtraction; natural subtraction is confined to bounded indices. ev is the divided-power vector, not a basis assertion. P=projector in the source is Y_ell X_ell, and integralMatrix is X_(ell−i) Q Y_(ell−j). In the pinned Mathlib, Module.End multiplication is composition (rightmost first), and 1 is identity. coeffProd and coeffOmit are the specified finite products, including empty product 1. latticeEnd is an actual scalar-restricted map when preservation holds and zero otherwise; T002 explicitly proves preservation and agreement for A, every divided power, and x,y,h, and proves the commutator and four-factor restriction identity. Consequently its fallback branch cannot silently replace the original operators under the theorem hypotheses. TensorLeft and TensorRight are the actual ℤ tensor products in the two orders. Pinned TensorProduct.comm swaps pure tensors; AddEquiv.module transports only the scalar action while preserving the existing additive group; AddEquiv.linearEquiv makes that very map linear. Pinned LinearMap.baseChange acts on the M factor of K⊗ℤM. Thus induced is conjugation of the correct base change, not an unrelated representation. T011 is an unconditional planned bridge proving the right-factor K-action, pure-tensor swap, induced evaluation and intertwining. T004 uses it to transport dimension, nonzeroness, matrix units and invariance back to the original order. These obligations suffice for both directions of the actual representation change; their bodies remain required at assembly. No construction field assumes P. Nontrivial means the tensor space is nonzero; stable and bottom/top express the stated subspaces. Invariance under x,y,h is equivalent to invariance under the prescribed L_K action by closure under K-linear combinations and evaluation on its three generators, without division by 2 or a faithfulness requirement.
